summary: Learn root cause analysis and CAPA with 5 Whys, Fishbone, and verification tools. Build audit-ready closure skills.
lede: Root cause analysis training is for professionals handling incidents, defects, audit findings, or process deviations who need to investigate problems and verify their causes. Participants practice framing problems with 5W2H, mapping causes with 5 Whys and Fishbone diagrams, and drafting CAPA registers. They also use evidence to assess likely causes and check corrective action effectiveness before documenting closure.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already handle incidents, defects, audit findings, or process deviations and now need a more disciplined method for investigation, cause verification, and corrective action closure. It suits roles that must turn evidence into action and action into documented proof of effectiveness. Quality Managers responsible for nonconformance closure and CAPA governance. Operations Supervisors handling repeat process deviations and containment actions. Internal Auditors reviewing findings, evidence trails, and closure effectiveness. Compliance Officers tracking corrective actions against control expectations. Process Improvement Specialists mapping causes and testing solutions. Production Engineers analyzing defects, downtime, and process variation. Incident Investigators documenting evidence and interviewing witnesses. Quality Assurance Analysts managing defect trends and verification records. Supplier Quality Engineers issuing and following supplier corrective actions. Management Review Coordinators preparing CAPA summaries for leadership.
modules: Causal Analysis with 5 Whys and Fishbone
prerequisites: You will need a laptop, spreadsheet software, and access to sample incident, defect, or nonconformance records for exercises. Prior experience with basic quality, operations, or compliance workflows is helpful; advanced statistics, programming, or specialized software are not required.
